transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Iran says it is ready for any renewed war wage by the U.S. and Israel.
Iranian state media said that the country was operating under the assumption that the U.S. and Israel would attack,
as NPR's Hadil Al-Shalchi reports.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araki told Iranian state media that just as his country is prepared for diplomacy,
it's prepared for war.
Araki said that "any scenario is conceivable, including the possibility of an attack by the U.S. and Israel."
The U.S. and Israel are preparing plans for a possible attack on Iran in early November,
according to a person briefed on the matter speaking to NPR in the condition of anonymity.
Iranian state media also quoted a security source saying that if Iranian officials or civilian infrastructure were attacked,
Iran would retaliate by targeting U.S. interests in the region,
as well as the infrastructure and assets of countries participating in the war.
Hadil Al-Shalchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
Minnesota Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar says she will move out of the Washington D.C. home that federal agents searched last week.
She told MS Now that the attention brought on by the raid has made her feel unsafe there.
Omar was born in Somalia and is a naturalized U.S. citizen.
She said in her first interview since the search that she's "confident in the fact that I didn't do anything wrong."
President Trump made gains with young voters in 2024,
but two years later, more than six in 10 Gen Z voters say their midterm vote this fall is in opposition to the president and his policies.
That's according to a new Harvard Youth Poll that surveyed more than 2,000 voters between the ages of 18 and 29,
and NPR's Ilhan Omar reports.
Democrats have a big advantage in the latest Harvard Youth Poll. Among Gen Zers who say they're definitely voting this fall,
63 percent plan to vote for Democrats,
compared to just a quarter voting Republican and one in 10 who are undecided.
There's also an enthusiasm gap, with more young Democrats than young Republicans saying they're definitely going to vote.
But overall, only one-third of Gen Z plans to vote,
which is down from 40 percent ahead of the 2018 and 2022 midterms.
What's more, most young people remain unhappy with the state of the country,
with just nine percent saying they feel the country is headed in the right direction.
A record low for the poll.
Ilhan Omar and PR News.
President Trump is heading to Iowa as the state's Republican Senate candidate is navigating a tricky political landscape in a tight race.
Congresswoman Ashley Hinson promises to support Trump when it benefits Iowa,
but also vows to push back when necessary.
She previously called herself Trump's top ally, but now says she'll be Iowa's best bipartisan fighter.
Her Democratic opponent, state lawmaker Josh Turek, also says he'll work with Trump on border security and other issues.
Major U.S. stock indexes fell today.
The S&P 500 fell more than one percent for its worst day since July.
The NASDAQ tumbled more than two and a half percent.
This is NPR.
An assessment of the world's coral reef ecosystems says almost all face a high risk of collapse in the next 50 years,
mostly due to warming oceans.
The International Union for Conservation of Nature's assessment found that 96 percent of shallow water reef systems
are already critically endangered and could collapse by 2075.
The French government says it is preparing vast security measures for Saturday's nationwide demonstrations.
As Eleanor Beardsley reports this week, the protesters are being led by what are known as the yellow vests,
a movement of white working-class voters that dogged President Emmanuel Macron during his first term.
Along with tens of thousands of police, security operations will be reinforced by Operation Sentinel,
a military contingent that patrolled French streets after the terrorist attacks in 2015.
President Macron held a security meeting this morning over the crisis that is casting a dark cloud over the waning days of his presidency.
Macron and his government are being blamed by the far left and far right
for letting the violence get out of control and for the underlying conditions motivating the protesters.
What began in mid-September as a student protest for improved facilities and more teachers
has ballooned into a general movement involving unions and public sector workers
against the high cost of living and what they say are growing inequalities.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
A city in South Korea is again trying to free a huge shark from a narrow canal. Workers in Busan had herded the shark nicknamed "Bukangi"
out of the canal yesterday after weeks of trial and error.
But Bukangi swam beneath a barrier net and re-entered the waterway today.
I'm Rylan Barton. This is NPR News.

topics.text: Iran says it is ready for war as U.S. and Israel reportedly prepare possible attack plans
Rep. Ilhan Omar says she will move out of Washington home searched by federal agents
Harvard Youth Poll finds Gen Z favors Democrats but overall voter enthusiasm and optimism are low
President Trump heads to Iowa as Senate race between Ashley Hinson and Josh Turek tightens
Major U.S. stock indexes fall, with the S&P 500 posting its worst day since July
IUCN assessment warns nearly all shallow-water coral reef systems could collapse by 2075
French government readies massive security measures ahead of nationwide yellow vest protests Saturday
Busan crews again attempt to free shark nicknamed Bukangi from narrow canal after it re-enters
